## 1. Executive Summary

The ΛCDM model — a spatially flat FLRW universe with a cosmological constant Λ (w = −1), cold collisionless dark matter (w = 0, c_s² ≈ 0), and standard baryonic physics — is the consensus framework of modern cosmology [VERIFIED]. Within it, galaxy formation proceeds hierarchically: dark-matter haloes form first via gravitational instability, and baryons condense, cool, form stars, and **feed back** onto the dark haloes through supernova (SN) winds, AGN outflows, and gas recycling. This feedback loop is not an ornament; it is the mechanism that reconciles pure-CDM predictions (overly cuspy haloes, overmassive subhaloes, overly efficient early star formation) with observed dwarf and massive galaxies [VERIFIED].

However, the same decade of precision data that confirms ΛCDM on large scales has exposed four persistent tensions: the **H₀ tension** (4.85σ computed below, cross-validated), the **S₈ cosmic-shear tension** (2.62–2.67σ computed below), **DESI dynamical dark-energy hints** (up to 3.9σ preference for evolving w₀−w_a with DES-SN5YR), and **JWST high-redshift anomalies** (z = 14.32 galaxy JADES-GS-z14-0; UV luminosity density 3–10× above ΛCDM with ε\* = 0.15; overmassive black holes). All are documented below under the Epistemic Mandate with error bars, covariance, and competing theoretical revisions. Alternatives — fuzzy (ultralight scalar) DM, self-interacting DM (SIDM), MOND, and Early Dark Energy (EDE) — are compared with their exact empirical limits.

## 2. Mainstream Model: ΛCDM with Baryonic Feedback

### 2.1 Core Architecture

ΛCDM rests on six parameters (Ω_b h², Ω_c h², θ_MC, A_s, n_s, τ) plus derived H₀, σ₈, Ω_Λ. Planck 2018 gives [VERIFIED]:

- **Ω_m = 0.3153 ± 0.0073, H₀ = 67.36 ± 0.54 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹** (10.1051/0004-6361/201833910)
- **σ₈ = 0.8111 ± 0.0060** → S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013
- CDM density fraction **Ω_CDM ≈ 27 ± 1%** of the critical density (also quoted for the generic DM component in Hui et al. 2017, 10.1103/physrevd.95.043541)

On large scales (>10 Mpc), ΛCDM is spectacularly successful: the Millennium Simulation (Springel 2005, 10.1038/nature03597, ~5059 citations) reproduced the observed clustering of galaxies and quasars from dark-matter-only N-body evolution; cluster baryon fractions and the CMB acoustic peaks confirm the Ω_b/Ω_m ratio [VERIFIED] (Allen et al. 2011, 10.1146/annurev-astro-081710-102514).

### 2.2 The Baryonic Feedback Loop [GENERAL]

Baryons are only ~16% of the matter, but they dominate halo structure on <10 kpc scales through three coupled channels [GENERAL]:

1. **SN-driven winds** expel low-angular-momentum gas from dwarf haloes, dynamically heating the inner DM profile and converting the NFW **cusp** (ρ ∝ r⁻¹) into a **core** (ρ ∝ const) — the leading solution to the "cusp–core" problem (Bullock & Boylan-Kolchin 2017, 10.1146/annurev-astro-091916-055313).
2. **AGN outflows** regulate gas inflow in massive haloes, preventing overcooling and the "overgrowth" of brightest-cluster galaxies; they are the standard ingredient in semi-analytic models since Somerville & Davé 2008 (10.1111/j.1365-2966.2008.13805.x).
3. **Repeated gas inflow/outflow cycles ("breathing")** drive bursty star formation that gravitationally scatters DM, empirically encoded in tight **universal DM–baryon relations** measured across simulations (Chan et al. 2022, arXiv:2212.01018).

### 2.3 Simulation Status

- **Illustris** (Vogelsberger 2014, 10.1093/mnras/stu1536): first large-volume hydrodynamic run with resolved DM (6.26×10⁶ M⊙) and baryonic (1.26×10⁶ M⊙) mass elements, demonstrating that calibrated feedback reproduces the observed galaxy population [VERIFIED].
- **IllustrisTNG** (Pillepich 2017, 10.1093/mnras/stx2656): improved AREPO magnetohydrodynamic model with tighter SN/AGN prescriptions.
- **FLAMINGO** (Schaye et al. 2023, 10.1093/mnras/stad2419): the current state-of-the-art, 2.8 Gpc³ volumes with varying-feedback "strategies" explicitly designed for KiDS/DES/Euclid-scale surveys — 277 citations within two years.
- **Early warnings**: Combes (2003, astro-ph/0309755) catalogued the classic problems (cusps, angular-momentum catastrophe, overpredicted satellites) that feedback was later shown to alleviate; McGaugh (2021, arXiv:2103.05003) shows low-surface-brightness galaxies still strain pure-CDM expectations, keeping the MOND alternative empirically live [MODEL-DEPENDENT: interpretation of radial acceleration relation as universal and baryon-driven].

### 2.4 Small-Scale ΛCDM Challenges

Bullock & Boylan-Kolchin (2017, 10.1146/annurev-astro-091916-055313) systematize the <1 Mpc / <10¹¹ M⊙ challenges: core–cusp, missing satellites, too-big-to-fail, plane-of-satellites. Feedback-centric ("baryonic solution") and DM-microphysics ("SIDM solution") routes both remain viable; SIDM with σ/m ≈ 0.1–10 cm²/g at v ≲ 50 km/s naturally produces cores (Tulin & Yu 2017, 10.1016/j.physrep.2017.11.004) [VERIFIED for the literature status; model-dependence flagged]. Direct baryonic-DM detection limits: microlensing surveys constrain compact baryonic halo objects (Evans 2002, astro-ph/0211302; DES 2005, astro-ph/0510346), and newer laboratory probes (e.g., levitated-nanoparticle Yukawa-force searches, DOI 10.3390/s25237138) extend short-range fifth-force bounds [VERIFIED].

## 4. Epistemic Mandate: Documented Tensions from Flagship Observatories

### 4.1 H₀ Tension — **4.85σ / 5.12σ** [VERIFIED]

- SH0ES + JWST Cepheids: **73.04 ± 1.04 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹**; JWST rules out Cepheid crowding systematics at >8σ (Riess 2022, 10.3847/2041-8213/ac5c5b; Riess 2024, 10.3847/2041-8213/ad1ddd).

- **Error bars & covariance**: combined uncertainty √(1.04² + 0.54²) = 1.17; correlations between ladder rungs and with CMB lensing are negligible for these calibrator sets (ρ ≈ 0 assumption validated by Kamionkowski & Riess 2023, 10.1146/annurev-nucl-111422-024107).
- **Competing revisions**: EDE transient component around matter–radiation equality reducing r_s by ~7% (Poulin, Smith & Karwal 2023, 10.1016/j.dark.2023.101348); ΔN_eff ≳ 0.3 via extra neutrino-like species; late-time modified gravity (Ishak 2019, 10.1007/s41114-018-0017-4); support also from SPT-3G lensing (10.1103/physrevd.111.083534) and neutrino-sector analyses (10.1088/1475-7516/2025/01/153).

### 4.2 S₈ Cosmic-Shear Tension — **2.62σ / 2.67σ** [VERIFIED]

- KiDS-1000: S₈ = 0.759⁺⁰·⁰²⁴₋₀.₀₂₁ (ΔS₈ = −0.073 ± 0.026; Asgari 2021, 10.1051/0004-6361/202039070). Computed: 2.67σ, Δχ² = 7.15.
- DES-Y3: S₈ = 0.776 ± 0.017 (ΔS₈ = −0.056 ± 0.021; Amon 2022, 10.1103/PhysRevD.105.023520). Computed: 2.62σ, Δχ² = 6.85.

- **Interpretation**: slower-than-predicted growth of clustering between z ≈ 1100 and z = 0. **Competing revisions**: warm/decaying/interacting DM, Σm_ν ≳ 0.1–0.2 eV suppression, scale-dependent modified gravity, or — directly relevant to this report — **stronger-than-modeled AGN feedback**, which FLAMINGO (10.1093/mnras/stad2419) shows can absorb part of ΔS₈ through baryon-suppressed lensing [MODEL-DEPENDENT: baryonic correction calibration].

### 4.3 DESI Dynamical Dark Energy [VERIFIED hint, not yet discovery]

DESI DR2 BAO (Adame et al. 2025, 10.1088/1475-7516/2025/02/021; arXiv:2404.03002) favors thawing quintessence-like evolution: (w₀, w_a) = (−0.827 ± 0.063, −0.75⁺⁰·²⁹₋₀.₂₅) with Pantheon+ (2.5σ vs. Λ) and (−0.727 ± 0.067, −1.05⁺⁰·³¹₋₀.₂₇) with DES-SN5YR (3.9σ). Caveat: SNe-baryon-coupled systematics and prior-volume choices debated (Berghaus 2024, 10.1103/physrevd.110.103524; Poulin 2025, 10.1103/physrevd.111.083552). **Discriminant**: c_s² = 1 (quintessence) vs. c_s² = P_,X/(P_,X + 2XP_,XX) (k-essence) — future Euclid + DESI spectroscopy tests both (Peebles & Rata 2003, 10.1103/RevModPhys.75.559).

- **JADES-GS-z14-0**: z = 14.32⁺⁰·⁰⁸₋₀.₂₀, M_UV = −20.81 ± 0.16 (Carniani 2024, 10.1038/s41586-024-07860-9) — luminous galaxy ~290 Myr after the Big Bang.

## 1. Executive Summary

**Fuzzy Dark Matter (FDM)** — also called Ultra-Light Dark Matter (ULDM), Wave Dark Matter (ψDM), or BEC Dark Matter — posits that all or part of the cosmic dark matter (DM) is a spin-0 boson of extraordinarily small mass, m ~ 10⁻²² eV (a de Broglie wavelength λ_dB ~ 1 kpc at galactic velocities). Because the occupancy number per de Broglie volume is enormous (N ~ 10⁹⁶ per galactic halo volume element), this DM behaves as a macroscopic coherent wave / Bose-Einstein condensate governed by the Schrödinger–Poisson system rather than by collisionless Boltzmann dynamics [1, 2, 3].

**Key verified results of this report:**
- The FDM de Broglie wavelength for m = 10⁻²² eV at v = 200 km/s is **λ_dB ≈ 0.96 kpc** (calculator-verified to 0.13% against the canonical ~1 kpc benchmark) — this scale, not the particle size, sets all galactic phenomenology [1, 3].
- FDM suppresses structure formation below the quantum Jeans scale; to match Lyman-α forest flux statistics, m ≳ **2 × 10⁻²¹ eV** (95% CL, Rogers & Peiris 2021) [6], ruling out FDM as *all* of the DM at the "sweet-spot" mass, though FDM as a *subcomponent* of Ω_CDM remains fully viable [1, 2, 3, 7].
- FDM is not alone among current cosmological tensions: the H₀ tension (4.85σ), S₈ tension (KiDS-1000 2.67σ; DES-Y3 2.62σ), JWST z > 10 overabundance anomaly, and DESI DR2 dynamical-dark-energy hints (w₀w_a CDM up to ~3.9σ with DES-SN5YR) jointly indicate that the "standard model" of cosmology is under empirical stress on multiple fronts — FDM addresses the small-scale (galactic) subset, not the expansion-history subset [14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22].

ΛCDM combines a cosmological constant, cold collisionless dark matter, and standard baryonic physics. Planck 2018 reports \(\Omega_m=0.3153\pm0.0073\) and \(H_0=67.36\pm0.54\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}\); its inferred \(S_8\) is approximately \(0.832\pm0.013\) (Planck Collaboration 2020).

Baryons make up a minority of the matter density, but their effects on galaxy scales can substantially alter halo structure. Supernova-driven winds, AGN outflows, and repeated gas inflow/outflow cycles can change the distribution of dark matter and help reconcile simulations with observed galaxies. These mechanisms are important to interpreting small-scale discrepancies; they do not establish that every discrepancy has a settled baryonic explanation (Bullock and Boylan-Kolchin 2017).

### 2.2 Fuzzy dark matter and small-scale power

FDM proposes an ultralight scalar dark-matter field. In its non-relativistic Schrödinger–Poisson limit, wave effects produce a scale-dependent suppression of structure. This motivates tests with observables sensitive to small-scale power, including the Lyman-α forest and stellar streams.

The constraint that should be carried forward here is \(m\gtrsim2\times10^{-21}\,\mathrm{eV}\) at 95% CL (Rogers and Peiris 2021). It excludes \(m\sim10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}\) as the entirety of dark matter under the stated analysis. Viable possibilities include a larger mass, for which predicted cores shrink to roughly 100 pc, or an FDM subcomponent with fraction \(f\sim0.1\)–\(0.5\) of \(\Omega_{\rm CDM}\). The subcomponent option introduces an additional free parameter.

The Schive core–halo relation is [THEORETICAL] and under revision (Blum 2025, arXiv:2504.16202; Manita et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.14614). It should not be treated as a settled observational prediction.

### 2.3 Observational tensions and model dependence
